s: The Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) derives its legal basis from which of the following provisions?
o: Article 262 and the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985
Article 315 and the Central Civil Services Act, 1985
Article 323A and the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985
Article 323B and the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021
x: CAT is empowered by Article 323A and was established under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985. It is a statutory and quasi-judicial body.
tq: Link the constitutional enabling provision with the parent statute instead of confusing Articles 323A and 323B.

s: The Central Administrative Tribunal was set up in 1985 during the Prime Ministership of:

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the eligibility of members of the Central Administrative Tribunal?
o: Judicial Members must be district judges, while Administrative Members must have served at the level of Joint Secretary only.
Judicial Members must be serving Supreme Court judges, while Administrative Members must be serving Cabinet Secretaries.
Judicial Members must be qualified as High Court judges, while Administrative Members must have served at the level of Additional Secretary or above.
Both categories of Members must be serving members of the Union Public Service Commission.
x: Judicial Members must possess qualifications equivalent to those of High Court judges. Administrative Members require service at the level of Additional Secretary or above.
tq: Separate the judicial and administrative eligibility streams rather than applying one qualification to both.

s:
With reference to the Central Administrative Tribunal, consider the following statements:
1. Its main Bench is located at New Delhi.
2. It has 18 outlying Benches.
3. It has jurisdiction over service disputes of civilian defence employees, but not armed forces personnel.
4. It exercises jurisdiction over notified public sector undertakings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements are correct. CAT has its main Bench at New Delhi and 18 outlying Benches, and its jurisdiction includes specified Central and All-India service matters, civilian defence employees and notified PSUs, but excludes armed forces personnel.
tq: Test jurisdiction by separating included civilian categories from the expressly excluded armed forces personnel.

s: Which of the following statements about the procedure followed by the Central Administrative Tribunal is correct?
o: It is strictly bound by the Code of Civil Procedure and prohibits personal appearance of litigants.
It is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, follows the principles of natural justice, charges nominal fees and permits parties to appear in person.
It is not bound by any legal principles and imposes court-level fees in every case.
It follows only criminal procedure and permits appearance only through senior advocates.
x: CAT is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure. It follows natural justice, charges nominal filing fees and permits litigants to appear in person.

President of India through a constitutional reference
Central Government through a departmental appeal

x: Article 323A covers recruitment and service conditions of public servants across the listed levels and permits Parliament alone to establish such tribunals.

Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

s:
With reference to the National Tribunals Commission proposed in the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It is proposed to have its headquarters at New Delhi.
2. It is proposed to have two judicial and two technical members in addition to the Chairperson.
3. Its functions include tribunal appointments, performance review and disciplinary inquiries.
4. Its Chairperson must be a serving judge of the Supreme Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Chairperson may be a former Supreme Court judge or a former High Court Chief Justice; the office is not restricted to a serving Supreme Court judge.
tq: Reject the over-specific authority qualification while retaining the organisational details.

A Chairperson and four technical members only
Two Chairpersons, two judicial members and one technical member

s: A tribunal is best described as a body which is:
o: Quasi-judicial, lying between an executive body and a court
A legislative committee exercising delegated law-making power
A constitutional court equal in status to the Supreme Court
Purely executive and without adjudicatory functions
x: A tribunal is quasi-judicial: it is neither purely executive nor a regular court, but occupies an intermediate position between the two.

s:
Which of the following is NOT generally regarded as a merit of administrative tribunals?
1. Expertise and specialisation
2. Speedier adjudication
3. Lower cost
4. Compulsory application of the full Civil Procedure Code
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Expertise, specialisation, speed and lower cost are recognised merits. Tribunals follow principles of natural justice instead of being bound by the full application of the Civil Procedure Code.
tq: Find the exception by separating tribunal advantages from the procedural feature that does not apply.

tq: Recognise the practical procedural distinction between tribunals and ordinary courts.

s: Which criticism of the tribunal system relates most directly to institutional independence?
o: The same ministries whose decisions are reviewed may administer the tribunals.
Tribunals are constitutionally prohibited from reviewing administrative action.
Tribunals cannot provide any form of adjudication.
x: A major criticism is that parent ministries, which may be litigants before tribunals, also administer them, creating concerns about executive control and independence.
tq: Match the criticism with the institutional conflict it describes.

s: Which statement best captures the constitutional position of tribunals in relation to High Courts?

Tribunals completely exclude the judicial-review jurisdiction of High Courts.
High Courts may review only the financial accounts of tribunals.
Tribunals may overrule constitutional decisions of High Courts.
x: Although tribunals provide specialised adjudication, their decisions remain subject to the judicial-review jurisdiction of High Courts.
tq: Reject the absolute-exclusion trap in statements about judicial review.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tribunals are intended to provide faster adjudication.
2. Tribunals are intended to bring specialised expertise into dispute resolution.
3. Tribunals are completely outside the supervisory jurisdiction of constitutional courts.
4. Parent ministries may face a conflict of interest when they administer tribunals dealing with their own decisions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Tribunals remain subject to judicial review by High Courts, so statement 3 is false.
tq: Combine merits, criticism and the judicial-review safeguard, rejecting the absolute claim.
